steps.title: Cap the persistent journal at 1G with a journald drop-in

edits.new:
# Written by stackward: plan step journald-cap, fixes LOG-001.
# Caps the persistent journal. Remove this file and restart
# systemd-journald to undo.
[Journal]
SystemMaxUse=1G
edits.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/90-stackward-journal-cap.conf
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+# Written by stackward: plan step journald-cap, fixes LOG-001.
+# Caps the persistent journal. Remove this file and restart
+# systemd-journald to undo.
+[Journal]
+SystemMaxUse=1G

commands.why: load the new limit; journald vacuums older files down to it

undo.description: Remove the drop-in and restart systemd-journald; the journal may then grow to the default limit again. Journal files already vacuumed are gone.

notes: Restarting systemd-journald drops no running service; journal files older than the 1G limit are deleted.

steps.title: Set the kernel hardening values with a sysctl drop-in

edits.new:
# Written by stackward: plan step sysctl-hardening, fixes KRN-002, KRN-003, KRN-004.
# Hardening values only: net.ipv4.ip_forward and the other settings
# Docker needs are never set here. Remove this file to undo at the
# next boot.
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 2
net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
kernel.kptr_restrict = 1
edits.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/etc/sysctl.d/90-stackward-hardening.conf
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+# Written by stackward: plan step sysctl-hardening, fixes KRN-002, KRN-003, KRN-004.
+# Hardening values only: net.ipv4.ip_forward and the other settings
+# Docker needs are never set here. Remove this file to undo at the
+# next boot.
+net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 2
+net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects = 0
+kernel.kptr_restrict = 1

commands.why: apply this drop-in now, and only this file, not the whole sysctl.d tree

undo.description: Remove the drop-in so the old values return at the next boot, and set the old running values now.

notes: /etc/sysctl.conf sets kernel.kptr_restrict = 0 and is read after this drop-in, so the old value returns at boot; change it there by hand.
/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=0 (want 1) and ufw applies it again on every enable and reload; this step leaves that file alone.

steps.title: Rotate json-file container logs (max-size 10m, max-file 3) in daemon.json

undo.description: Put the previous daemon.json back (its content is the old side of this step's diff; apply also keeps a copy under /var/backups/stackward/<run-id>/) and restart Docker.

notes: Restarting Docker stops and starts every container unless live-restore is on; containers without a restart policy stay stopped.
The limits apply to containers created after the restart; recreate running containers (for example docker compose up -d --force-recreate) to rotate their logs.
